hypothesis.preserved_v6_state: Ordinary FAR still requires exclusive rejection origin: rejection_seed=true and acceptance_seed=false.
hypothesis.causal_defect: AAC is confirmed only after outside acceptance, one causal defended pullback and a later completed reacceleration. The inherited adapter then rests a second order at that already-defended pullback. A fill is therefore conditional on a new deep return which can itself be evidence that the confirmed initiative is failing.
hypothesis.single_strategy_change: At completed AAC reacceleration, the confirmation leg owns entry. Submit a market parent only when the unchanged source-boundary stop, live external objective and declared taker/stop/maker costs preserve the existing structural-R contract. Otherwise terminate; never fall back to a second pullback limit.
hypothesis.unchanged: Liquidity detection, acceptance confirmation, pool identity, draw resolution, target, source-boundary invalidation, market-leadership semantics, costs, current-NAV 3% sizing, session I7 module, global arbitration and NautilusTrader execution/accounting are unchanged.
hypothesis.interpretation_rule: L1 was already inspected. It is reused only to isolate AAC entry ownership and cannot establish success regardless of performance.

research_question: After preserving v6 auction-origin ownership, does assigning AAC entry to the already-confirmed reacceleration leg remove second-pullback adverse selection without inventing a new target, stop, filter or execution model?

selection.method: Controlled replay of the previously inspected Candidate 14 L1 interval. V6 is the baseline; only AAC entry ownership changes. This interval is permanently ineligible for a success claim or future holdout use.

strategy_change_control.single_change: confirmed AAC reacceleration owns market entry; second pullback fallback prohibited
